note: The hand-written (literal WSP) releases this deployment serves: one entry per release, its bytes in models/<hex>/ beside this file. Adding a release is a new entry plus its registry directory (and a rebuild only when it needs a forward this build does not have). Every score is a development number as the authoring lane reported it, with its source; no test-partition score is listed. Text from docs/wsp/README.md, docs/wsp/RESULTS_GEN6.md and the model cards (feat/handwritten-science).

releases.forecasts: The diameter of a free-floating burning methanol droplet after the cutoff (quantiles), from its conditions and the diameters measured before the cutoff; the droplet may stay in a hot flame, go to a cool flame or lose its flame.
releases.authorship_note: Third generation: typed after reading the methanol train partition and a train-only audit of D2. Not replaced by the fourth or fifth generation.

scores.metric: CRPS of the droplet diameter, FLEX methanol validation partition
scores.comparison: best fitted model 77.7 µm; zero-shot flex.wsp W0 50.4 µm
scores.source: docs/wsp/README.md, table of the carried models

limits: Tracker artefacts (glare, soot, bubbles, dropouts, frozen values) are scored as data; no model forecasts them (about a third of the train error).
A flame that went out less than a second before the cutoff still reads as burning.
The helium term of the clock rests on three runs.
The radiative clock above the critical diameter rests on CO2-diluted pairs; if the critical diameter in CO2 is off, the slope is wrong between atmospheres.

scores.metric: Integrated Brier score 6–120 s, CFI-G validation, ethane/propane/butane, without the planned stop: extinction / flow termination
Flame Design validation days, ethylene as itself: without / with the planned stop (extinction / flow termination)

limits: On CFI-G validation with the planned stop it is worse than the model before it (sum 0.2271 against 0.2191, two sessions).
On the Flame Design validation days every normal-flame case ended by a flow stop, so extinction there only measures false extinction; two or three validation days are few.
A nitrogen-diluted ethylene flame lives longer than the growth law says; ethylene below 1900 K is refused.
The endpoint method misplaces the flow change on tests with an ignition-to-test ramp.

releases.inputs_note: No stored BASS run carries x_o2, a width in metres and the fan history, so on stored runs this release refuses. Forecast it on a typed scenario: conditions, flow stages and a few tip positions before the cutoff. Its development score is in sample widths, from the lane's track files.

scores.metric: CRPS of the flame tip, 12 BASS burns measured blind from the videos
scores.source: docs/wsp/README.md, table of the carried models

scores.comparison: a constant scores 0.125: the quench boundary fails

limits: No run has a length calibration: its scores are in sample widths; the metric route needs a width in metres and is tested on a synthetic fixture only.
Twelve burns of three sessions of one campaign.
Flows above 11 cm/s, 21 % oxygen and the narrow sample are outside train.
The quench law is wrong on spread-or-not: read no ignition forecast from it.
Not predicted: temperature, flame brightness, the flame base.
